items.q: If the body is ~70% water, why does plain drinking water feel temporary?
items.a: Almost none of body water is free liquid — most is **crystalline cellular water**, a gel/Jell-O structure around proteins that stores plant "light"/solar energy. Pure bottled water hydrates briefly then **exits in ~45 minutes** because without salts, minerals, and proteins it never becomes **cellular gel**.

items.q: How does Bush link biologic age to hydration structure?
items.a: He says biologic age and disease risk **correlate with how much crystal water you hold**. That gel reservoir is the battery for solar energy liberated from **plant carbon-chain foods** — lose the structure, lose vitality.

sections.title: Phase angle and cancer as late signal

items.q: What phase-angle numbers does Bush use as a vitality dial?
items.a: Ideal health ~**10–12**, clinic healthy ~**7–8**, cancer ~**4**, death ~**3.5**. Cancer shows up near the floor of **cellular water energetics**, framed as a late **energetic disconnect** from plant/chlorophyll/sunlight signaling — not the root cause.

items.q: How does glyphosate fit Bush's chronic-disease story?
items.a: He ties the **1992–2002** Western chronic-disease spike to ~**4 billion pounds** of glyphosate sprayed globally. As a patented antibiotic/antifungal/antiparasite, it **dissolves cell–cell boundaries**, driving immune overactivation and "leaky" cells that leak light/water — deeper than classic **leaky gut**.

items.q: What is "upstream" of vitamins in his repair model?
items.a: **Redox signaling**: small carbon molecules from the microbiome act as a **wireless injury→repair network**. Cancer is framed as ~**20,000 unrepaired genetic injuries** from lost cell communication, not a missing multivitamin.

sections.title: Soil, food forests, and supply-chain risk

items.q: Why does Bush treat soil biodiversity as a health intervention?
items.a: A teaspoon of soil can hold more organisms than **humans on Earth**. **Soil = gut = life matrix** — biodiversity vs monoculture is the health/demise axis. Chemical farming is "ICU care for dead dirt"; regenerative ag (Farmers Footprint) grows life instead of killing weeds.

items.q: What food-system vulnerabilities does he highlight?
items.a: US chains can run **~3,000 miles**; **Los Angeles has ~3 days** of shelf stock. **40M acres** of lawn vs **120M** farmland — converting Kentucky bluegrass to **food forests** is framed as homeland-security-level resilience, echoing FDR: the nation's future is in its soil.
